title: The Annunciation: First Joyful Mystery
summary: Pray the First Joyful Mystery page by page: the story of the Annunciation, the Gospel, the decade prayers, and a quiet reflection.
coverAlt: Murillo's painting of the Annunciation: the angel Gabriel kneels before Mary, who looks up from her prayer.

pages.title: The Annunciation
pages.body: In a small town called Nazareth, the angel Gabriel brought Mary a message from God: she would be the mother of Jesus, the Son of the Most High. Mary was surprised, but she trusted God and said yes. As we pray this decade, we think of her humble yes, and we ask for a heart like hers.
pages.imageAlt: Murillo's painting of the Annunciation: the angel Gabriel kneels before Mary, who looks up from her prayer.

evidence.claim: Original child-friendly meditation on the mystery; the mystery and its traditional day follow the standard Rosary order.

pages.title: From the Gospel
pages.body:
God's Word tells us this mystery. From the Gospel according to Luke, chapter 1 (Douay-Rheims Bible):

“And the angel being come in, said unto her: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. … And the angel said to her: Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God. Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son; and thou shalt call his name Jesus. … And Mary said: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word.”

(Luke 1:26-38)

evidence.claim: Scripture quotation reproduced word for word from the Douay-Rheims 1899 American Edition (public domain); verse numbers omitted for reading aloud and ellipses mark skipped verses.

pages.title: Praying the Decade
pages.body:
We announce the mystery: The Annunciation, the First Joyful Mystery. Then we pray one decade of the Rosary, holding this scene in our hearts.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. (We pray the Hail Mary ten times, once for each bead of the decade.)

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell; lead all souls to Heaven, especially those in most need of Thy mercy.

evidence.claim: The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers use the standard formulas printed across this site.

pages.title: The Fruit of This Mystery: Humility and surrender to God
pages.body:
This mystery grows the fruit of humility and surrender to God. Mary said yes to God in a very ordinary moment. What is one small yes God might be asking of you today? Before the day ends, say it quietly, the way Mary did.

Let us pray: Lord Jesus, give us a humble heart like Mary's, ready to do whatever you ask. Amen. Our Lady of the Rosary, pray for us.

evidence.claim: Original reflection and closing prayer; the fruit of the mystery follows the traditional list used across this site.
